topic: ICSE 10th Board Section A - Part 1: Multiple Choice Questions (Marks: 20)

questions.question: Which of the following integer data types has the widest range in Java?
questions.explanation: 'long' occupies 8 bytes (64 bits), providing the largest range among Java's integer primitive types.

questions.question: Which Character class method checks if a passed character is neither a letter nor a digit?
questions.explanation: Java does not provide an isSpecial() method; inverting Character.isLetterOrDigit() identifies special symbols and punctuation.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method Math.cbrt()?
questions.explanation: Math.cbrt() computes the cube root of a number and returns the result as a double precision value.

questions.question: What is the value of the expression Math.round(7.5f)?
questions.explanation: Math.round() with a float argument returns an int rounded to the nearest integer, rounding 7.5 up to 8.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to call a superclass constructor explicitly from a subclass constructor?
questions.explanation: The 'super()' statement invokes the direct parent class constructor and must be the first statement in the subclass constructor.

questions.question: What is the result of the expression 13 & 9 in Java bitwise operations?
questions.explanation: 13 in binary is 1101 and 9 is 1001. Performing bitwise AND (1101 & 1001) produces 1001, which is 9.

questions.question: What does the method "Computer".indexOf('e', 3) return?
questions.explanation: The method searches starting from index 3: 'p'(3), 'u'(4), 'e'(5). It finds 'e' at index 5.

questions.question: What kind of copy is made when an array reference variable is assigned to another array variable (e.g., b = a)?
questions.explanation: Assigning array references duplicates only the memory pointer to the existing heap array, creating an alias without duplicating array elements[cite: 2].

questions.question: Which of the following is an invalid identifier in Java?
questions.explanation: Java identifiers cannot begin with a numeric digit.

questions.question: What does the method "Malayalam".lastIndexOf('a') return?
questions.explanation: Indexing 'M'(0), 'a'(1), 'l'(2), 'a'(3), 'y'(4), 'a'(5), 'l'(6), 'a'(7), 'm'(8). The last occurrence of 'a' is at index 7.

questions.question: Which memory area holds objects and arrays instantiated via the 'new' keyword?
questions.explanation: In Java, all objects and arrays allocated dynamically at runtime reside in Heap memory.

questions.question: What will Math.floor(-2.1) return?
questions.explanation: Math.floor() returns the largest double value less than or equal to the argument; -3.0 is less than -2.1.

questions.question: What is the ASCII value of character literal '0'?
questions.explanation: In the standard ASCII table, digit '0' is mapped to decimal code 48.

questions.question: Which statement can be used inside a switch construct to handle cases not matched by any explicit case constant?
questions.explanation: The 'default' label inside a switch block executes when no explicit case constant matches the selector expression.

questions.question: What is the return type of the method Character.toLowerCase(char ch)?
questions.explanation: Character.toLowerCase() returns the lowercase character representation as a primitive char.

questions.question: What is the default value of an uninitialized element in a char array in Java?
questions.explanation: Primitive char fields and array elements default to the null character literal '\u0000' (ASCII 0).

questions.question: What does the expression Math.ceil(-0.8) produce?
questions.explanation: Math.ceil(-0.8) yields mathematical zero preserved as negative floating point -0.0.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the function of the 'trim()' method in the String class?
options: Removes all spaces everywhere inside a string
Removes leading and trailing whitespace only
Truncates a string to half its length
questions.answer: Removes leading and trailing whitespace only
questions.explanation: The trim() method strips leading and trailing whitespace while leaving internal whitespace intact[cite: 2].

questions.question: Which operator has lower precedence than standard relational operators (<, >, <=, >=)?
questions.explanation: Equality operators (==, !=) have lower precedence than relational inequality operators (<, >, <=, >=).

questions.question: What exception is generated when an attempt is made to invoke a method on an object reference holding null?
questions.explanation: Attempting to dereference a null pointer by accessing instance members throws a java.lang.NullPointerException.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this single-character assignment:
options: char can store only a single character literal within single quotes
questions.answer: char can store only a single character literal within single quotes
questions.explanation: A char literal must represent exactly one character; two digits ('99') make it invalid character syntax[cite: 2].

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this array size initialization:
options: Array creation expression requires an explicit dimension size inside brackets
questions.answer: Array creation expression requires an explicit dimension size inside brackets
questions.explanation: When allocating an array without an initializer list, the size must be declared in square brackets (e.g., new int[5]).

questions.question: Identify the logical flaw in this loop intended to run 10 times:
options: Geometric doubling (i = i * 2) runs only 4 times (1, 2, 4, 8) instead of 10 linear steps
i = i * 2 is invalid inside for headers
questions.answer: Geometric doubling (i = i * 2) runs only 4 times (1, 2, 4, 8) instead of 10 linear steps
questions.explanation: To iterate 10 consecutive times, the loop counter should increment linearly (i++) rather than doubling.

questions.question: Identify the library method error:
options: name must be instantiated with new
len must be of type long
questions.explanation: The standard method in java.lang.String to inspect total character count is length()[cite: 1].

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this switch variable type:
options: switch expressions cannot evaluate floating-point types (float or double)
questions.answer: switch expressions cannot evaluate floating-point types (float or double)
questions.explanation: In Java, switch statements do not support floating-point expressions (float or double).

questions.question: Identify the logical error in this parity check:
options: num % 2 != 0 detects odd numbers but prints 'Even'
!= is invalid syntax in if expressions
questions.answer: num % 2 != 0 detects odd numbers but prints 'Even'
questions.explanation: An integer is even if num % 2 == 0; checking != 0 tests for odd parity, inverting the message logic.

questions.question: Identify the error in this Wrapper method call:
options: Method name must follow camelCase: parseBoolean()
true cannot be passed as a string
questions.answer: Method name must follow camelCase: parseBoolean()
questions.explanation: Java methods follow case-sensitive camelCase; the correct method is parseBoolean() with a capital 'B'.

questions.question: Identify the syntax error in this interface declaration:
options: Cannot use both 'class' and 'interface' keywords together in the declaration header
questions.answer: Cannot use both 'class' and 'interface' keywords together in the declaration header
questions.explanation: An interface header uses 'public interface Actionable', not 'public class interface'.
